title: Cartesian pushout-product axiom for categorical equivalences
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products and pushouts in a fixed universe, and categorical equivalences and the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. For degreewise injective simplicial maps $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $b:C\hookrightarrow D$, the cartesian pushout-product
$$a\mathbin\square b:(B\times C)\amalg_{A\times C}(A\times D)\longrightarrow B\times D$$
is degreewise injective. If either $a$ or $b$ is a categorical equivalence, then $a\mathbin\square b$ is a categorical equivalence. These assertions concern the unmarked Joyal model structure, not only inner-anodyne maps, and all constructions stay in the input universe.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 (printed p.92, PDF p.110): products preserve categorical equivalences, together with the trivial-cofibration weak factorization system of Theorem 2.2.5.1. The Cartesian axiom follows by pushing out a×C and applying two-out-of-three to a×D. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED archive. No Stacks tag states the unmarked Joyal-model assertion.

proof.text: Put $P=(B\times C)\amalg_{A\times C}(A\times D)$ and write $k:P\to B\times D$ for the displayed map. In degree $n$, injectivity of $a_n,b_n$ identifies the two summands with subsets of $B_n\times D_n$. Their intersection is precisely the image of $A_n\times C_n$: an equality $(x,b_n(c))=(a_n(t),y)$ forces $x=a_n(t)$ and $y=b_n(c)$, with unique $t,c$. Consequently the set pushout is their union, and $k_n$ is its inclusion. These identifications commute with every simplicial operator, so $k$ is degreewise injective, hence a cofibration by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure].

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1(C); elementary degreewise union computation of the cartesian pushout product.

proof.text: We first derive the needed product preservation, rather than assume the cartesian model axiom. For any simplicial set $K$ and any quasicategory $Q$ in a sufficiently large test universe, [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test] says $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ is a quasicategory. There is a natural simplicial isomorphism $\operatorname{Fun}(X\times K,Q)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(X,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q))$: a simplex on either side is the same map $X\times K\times\Delta^n\to Q$, after permuting factors. Explicitly the forward map sends $f$ to the map whose value on $x\in X_m$, $t:[m]\to[n]$ is the simplex $K\times\Delta^m\to Q$ given by $(z,s:[r]\to[m])\mapsto f_r(X(s)x,z,ts)$; evaluation at the identity simplex gives the inverse. Thus the isomorphism commutes with restriction in $X$. If $v:X\to Y$ is a categorical equivalence, testing it on the quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ makes the homotopy-category restriction for $v\times\mathrm{id}_K$ an equivalence, by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Since this holds for every $Q$, that same node identifies $v\times\mathrm{id}_K$ as a categorical equivalence. No fibrancy or nonemptiness of $K,X,Y$ was used.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92 / PDF page 110; agent proof via the hFun testing definition and explicit currying, in place of the source rigidification argument.

proof.text: Assume $a$ is a categorical equivalence. Step 2 gives categorical equivalences $a\times\mathrm{id}_C$ and $a\times\mathrm{id}_D$; both are degreewise injective, hence trivial cofibrations by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $u:A\times D\to P$ be the pushout of $a\times\mathrm{id}_C$ along $\mathrm{id}_A\times b$. We verify directly that $u$ is a trivial cofibration using that node's weak factorization system. Given a Joyal fibration $p:E\to F$ and a square from $u$ to $p$, restrict its lower map along $B\times C\to P$ and its upper map along $A\times C\to A\times D$. They form a square from $a\times\mathrm{id}_C$ to $p$. A lift $B\times C\to E$ exists because that map is a trivial cofibration. Its restriction on $A\times C$ agrees with the given map $A\times D\to E$. The pushout universal property therefore gives a map $P\to E$ extending both maps. Its composite with $p$ is the specified map $P\to F$, since they agree on both summands. This solves every lifting square for $u$ against every Joyal fibration. The converse lifting characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $u$ a trivial cofibration, in particular a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Corollary 2.2.5.4; elementary cobase-change lifting argument written out.

proof.text: The composite $k\circ u$ is $a\times\mathrm{id}_D$, as checked on $(t,d)\in A_n\times D_n$ in every degree. Both $u$ and $k\circ u$ are categorical equivalences by steps 2-3, so two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] makes $k$ a categorical equivalence. If instead $b$ is a categorical equivalence, interchange $(A,B,a)$ with $(C,D,b)$ and use the same argument. The flip $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$ identifies both product targets and both pushout diagrams, hence identifies the resulting pushout-product map with $k$ up to simplicial isomorphism. Such isomorphisms induce isomorphisms of all the testing categories, so preserve categorical equivalences. All products and pushouts used to form $P,k,u$ are degreewise finite products, disjoint unions and quotients of small sets, hence stay in the input universe. The auxiliary test $Q$ and its functor simplicial sets may lie in any sufficiently large universe, exactly as permitted in the categorical-equivalence definition; they change none of these constructions.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 with Theorem 2.2.5.1: two-out-of-three, symmetry and universe bookkeeping.

Step 3: u is the cobase change of the trivial cofibration ax id_C. I checked the explicit lift, the gluing through the pushout and both triangles; the model-structure statement makes the trivial cofibrations exactly the maps with the left lifting property against fibrations. Step 4: k∘u = ax id_D, so two-out-of-three gives k; the b case follows by the flip isomorphism.
